name: china-nexus
keyCapabilities: Zero‑day exploitation of network edge devices (FortiOS CVE‑2025‑21590)
Deployment of custom TINYSHELL backdoors on Juniper routers
Use of VMware vCenter/ESXi CVEs for privileged command execution
Memory injection into legitimate processes to bypass veriexec
Extraction and decryption of credentials from vCenter databases
Lateral movement via compromised ESXi hosts or vSphere environments
Persistence through registry Run keys, Windows services, Linux systemd units
Defense‑evasion via DLL sideloading, timestomping, RC4/AES‑HMAC encryption
Multi‑channel C2 communications (SOCKS5 relays, DNS‑over‑HTTPS tunnels, compromised VPNs)
Long dwell times up to five years in target sectors

description: China‑Nexus (also known as UNC3886/UNC5174, LuckyMouse, etc.) is a highly sophisticated espionage-focused group that exploits zero‑day vulnerabilities in critical network and virtualization assets to gain footholds in high‑value sectors worldwide. Their tactics blend device‑level backdoors on Juniper routers, long‑lived persistence via rootkits on end hosts, and covert C2 channels that leverage compromised VPNs and cloud services. The result is sustained access, often lasting years, used to exfiltrate IP, infrastructure data, and strategic intelligence.
goals: China‑Nexus seeks long‑duration access to strategic sectors worldwide, focusing on critical infrastructure, telecommunications, defense, energy, aerospace, healthcare, maritime and manufacturing. The group’s strategic objectives are primarily intelligence gathering—acquiring intellectual property, supply‑chain information, national security data—and enabling future cyber‑operations by maintaining dormant footholds. Their targeting profile leans toward organizations that host large amounts of sensitive or regulated data across multiple domains, leveraging the ability to infiltrate both physical network devices and virtualized environments.
